banh-beo-chay-hue.name: Hue Vegetarian Bánh Bèo
aliases: Hue steamed rice cakes with mung bean
banh-beo-chay-hue.serving_basis: About 16 small cups of steamed rice cake, four per person, served as a snack or shared dish.
banh-beo-chay-hue.description: Hue vegetarian bánh bèo is steamed in small cups and topped with mung beans cooked in annatto oil, crisp fried bread, sautéed leek and seaweed. Bếp Việt scales a home batch from the vegetarian topping described by Khám Phá Huế; serve with plant-based fish sauce or soy sauce.
banh-beo-chay-hue.finished_dish: Soft white rice cakes with a slight dimple, topped with nutty mung beans, crisp bread and seaweed; served with a gently sweet vegetarian dip.
banh-beo-chay-hue.serving: Drizzle a little leek oil and dipping sauce over each cup, then add the seaweed just before eating to keep it crisp. Serve warm.
tips: Soak the mung beans until tender, steam and mash them before sautéing; the topping should be fluffy rather than wet.
Rest the batter for at least 30 minutes and stir again before pouring so the cakes steam evenly.
Preheat the cups in the steamer, keep the water at a vigorous boil and steam in small batches.
Use clearly labeled plant-based bánh mì and vegetarian fish sauce if preparing a fully vegan meal.
banh-beo-chay-hue.image_alt: Small Hue vegetarian bánh bèo cups topped with mung beans, fried bread, leek and seaweed, served with a vegetarian dipping sauce.
banh-beo-chay-hue.time_note: About 3 hours 20 minutes, including 2 hours to soak the mung beans; the batter-resting time overlaps with the soak.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Use finely milled rice flour for soft, white cakes.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Adds a little chew; the local source describes adding a small amount to the batter.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Whisk into the batter until smooth and lump-free.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, steam and mash or blend.

ingredients.name: Bread
ingredients.notes: Cut into small cubes and fry or bake until crisp.

ingredients.name: Dried seaweed
ingredients.notes: Crumble and add at the end; optional.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Finely slice; sauté the white part and thinly slice the green part.

ingredients.name: Annatto oil
ingredients.notes: Use to sauté the mung beans and color the topping.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing leek, coating cups and frying the bread.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the batter and mung bean topping.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a plant-based product; diluted soy sauce is another option.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: For a gently sweet dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Slice or mince; optional.

preparation_steps: Soak the mung beans in clean water for about 2 hours, rinse and drain. Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, salt and water until smooth; rest for 30 minutes, then stir again.
Finely slice the leek. Cut the bread into small cubes; prepare the seaweed, small cups and steamer. Mix the vegetarian fish sauce with water and sugar to taste.
cooking_steps: Steam the mung beans until soft, then mash or blend. Sauté the white leek in annatto oil, add the mung beans and stir until fluffy; season with some of the salt.
Fry or bake the bread cubes until golden and crisp. Sauté the remaining leek in cooking oil to make leek oil.

Lightly oil the preheated bánh bèo cups. Pour batter to about halfway up each cup, place in a steamer over vigorously boiling water and steam for about 6–8 minutes, until set with a slight dimple in the center.
Let the cakes cool slightly, drizzle with a little leek oil and top with mung beans and crisp bread. Add seaweed just before serving with vegetarian dipping sauce.

banh-nam-chay-hue.name: Hue Vegetarian Bánh Nậm
aliases: Hue bánh nậm with mung bean
banh-nam-chay-hue.serving_basis: About 12 small banana-leaf bánh nậm, three per person.
banh-nam-chay-hue.description: Hue vegetarian bánh nậm are flat parcels of smooth white rice batter wrapped in banana leaves around mashed mung beans. Bếp Việt selects the mung-bean filling reported by VnExpress and scales the batter and steaming method for four; serve with soy sauce and chili.
banh-nam-chay-hue.finished_dish: Thin, soft, smooth cakes with a golden, nutty mung-bean center and a light banana-leaf aroma; served with vegetarian soy sauce.
banh-nam-chay-hue.serving: Serve in the leaf or unwrap onto a plate. Dip in soy sauce with chili and eat warm.
tips: Mash the mung beans into a cohesive paste with few hard pieces so it is easy to spread inside the thin cake.
Stir the batter constantly over low heat until thickened before spreading it on the leaves; a runny batter can spill over the edges.
Fold the leaves into flat parcels rather than making thick bundles so the batter cooks evenly.
Use banana leaves and soy sauce labeled as plant-based if preparing a fully vegan meal.
banh-nam-chay-hue.image_alt: Hue vegetarian bánh nậm wrapped in banana leaves, with one parcel opened to show golden mung bean filling in white rice batter.
banh-nam-chay-hue.time_note: About 3 hours 20 minutes, including 2 hours to soak the mung beans; the beans can be soaked ahead.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Use fine rice flour for a soft wrapper.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Helps the batter hold together when wrapped.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Whisk with the flours while cold, then cook into a thick batter.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak, steam until tender and mash for the filling; this version keeps mung beans as the main filling.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Divide between the batter, filling and coating the banana leaves.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the batter and mung bean filling.

ingredients.name: Banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse, wipe dry, soften briefly over heat and cut into wrapping pieces.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Dilute with warm water for dipping; choose a plant-based product.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Slice into the dipping sauce; optional.

preparation_steps: Soak the mung beans in clean water for about 2 hours, rinse and drain. Rinse and wipe the banana leaves, soften them briefly over heat and cut into wrappers.
Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, salt, oil and cold water until smooth. Mash the soaked mung beans or set them aside to steam.
cooking_steps: Steam the mung beans for about 20–25 minutes until tender, then mash and season with some of the salt. Warm a little oil in a pan and stir the paste until cohesive and fairly dry.
Set the batter pan over low heat and stir constantly until the mixture is smooth and just thickened. Turn off the heat but keep stirring so it does not catch on the bottom.

Brush a thin film of oil on the inside of a banana leaf. Spread a thin strip of batter, place a small spoonful of mung bean in the center, cover with a little more batter and fold into a flat rectangular parcel.
Arrange the parcels in a steamer over boiling water and steam for about 15–20 minutes, until the batter is opaque and cooked through. Rest briefly, then serve with soy sauce and chili.

banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.name: Hue Vegetarian Bánh Bột Lọc
banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.serving_basis: About 20 small banana-leaf tapioca cakes, five per person.
banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.description: Hue vegetarian bánh bột lọc have a chewy, translucent tapioca wrapper around tofu, wood-ear mushroom and carrot sautéed with leek. Bếp Việt follows the specific filling and method in VnExpress Cooking and the local technique described by Huế Ngày Nay; wrap in banana leaves, steam and serve with soy sauce.
banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.finished_dish: Small, chewy translucent cakes with a fragrant tofu and vegetable filling, served with savory-sweet soy sauce and optional chili.
banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.serving: Serve hot in their banana leaves with a small bowl of diluted soy sauce. Add fried leek if desired; avoid shrimp crackers for a fully vegan meal.
tips: Press excess moisture from the tofu so the filling does not release water inside the parcel.
Sauté the carrot and wood-ear mushrooms first to remove their raw aroma, then season with tofu and leek.
Pour boiling water into the tapioca starch gradually, stirring as you go; knead only after the dough has cooled enough to handle.
Wrap the banana leaves securely and steam until translucent. If boiling unwrapped cakes, test one first to gauge the texture.
banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.image_alt: Translucent Hue vegetarian bánh bột lọc wrapped in banana leaves, showing tofu, carrot and wood-ear mushroom filling, with soy sauce.
banh-bot-loc-chay-hue.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 15 minutes to soak the wood-ear mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Gradually add boiling water to partially cook the starch, then knead until smooth.

ingredients.name: Boiling water
ingredients.notes: Add a little at a time; adjust slightly for the absorbency of the starch.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Press dry, then crumble or dice finely.

ingredients.name: Dried wood-ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until pliable, rinse well and dice.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into small dice.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Finely slice the white and green parts; divide between the filling and optional finishing oil.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the filling and brushing the banana leaves.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: For the vegetarian dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: A little balances the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the dough and filling moderately.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the filling; reduce or omit to taste.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Choose a product without animal-derived ingredients.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Slice into the dipping sauce; optional.

ingredients.name: Banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse, wipe dry, soften over heat and cut into wrapping pieces.

preparation_steps: Soak the dried wood-ear mushrooms in warm water for 15 minutes, rinse well and dice. Press the tofu dry; finely dice the carrot and leek.
Rinse, wipe and soften the banana leaves. Bring water to a boil for the dough; prepare soy sauce, sugar and chili for dipping.
cooking_steps: Sauté the carrot and wood-ear mushrooms in a little oil for 2–3 minutes to remove their raw aroma. Add the tofu, white leek, soy sauce, salt, pepper and vegetarian seasoning powder; cook until fairly dry and let cool slightly.
Mix the tapioca starch with salt and oil. Gradually pour in the boiling water while stirring with a wooden spoon. When cool enough to handle, knead until smooth, elastic and no longer sticky.
Divide the dough into about 20 portions, flatten each, add a little filling and seal. Set each cake on an oiled banana-leaf piece, fold into a small parcel and arrange in a steamer.
Steam over boiling water for about 10–12 minutes until the dough turns translucent and the filling is hot. Mix soy sauce with a little warm water and sugar, add chili if desired and serve hot.

banh-ram-it-chay-hue.name: Hue Vegetarian Bánh Ram Ít
aliases: Hue bánh ít ram with vegetarian filling
banh-ram-it-chay-hue.serving_basis: About 12 pieces, each a soft stuffed sticky-rice cake on a crisp ram base, three per person.
banh-ram-it-chay-hue.description: Vegetarian bánh ram ít pairs a soft, chewy glutinous-rice dumpling with a crisp base made from steamed and fried glutinous-rice dough. Bếp Việt uses tofu, wood-ear mushroom, carrot and leek, drawing on the plant-based fillings described by Huế Ngày Nay for Hue cakes. This is an editorial variation, not a claim that there is only one traditional filling.
banh-ram-it-chay-hue.finished_dish: A golden crisp base supports a chewy sticky-rice dumpling filled with peppery tofu and vegetables; served with chili soy sauce.
banh-ram-it-chay-hue.serving: Place the stuffed bánh ít on the ram base just before serving so the base stays crisp. Serve warm with vegetarian soy sauce.
tips: Divide the glutinous-rice dough between the plain ram bases and the stuffed bánh ít; cover unused dough with a damp towel so it does not dry out.
Cook the filling until dry before wrapping so the dumplings do not split during steaming.
Let the steamed bases cool and dry before frying for a crisper finish.
The tofu, wood-ear and carrot filling is Bếp Việt’s editorial choice; mashed mung beans can be used instead.
banh-ram-it-chay-hue.image_alt: Hue vegetarian bánh ram ít with a white vegetable-filled sticky-rice dumpling on a crisp golden ram base, finished with fried leek.
banh-ram-it-chay-hue.time_note: About 1 hour 35 minutes, including 15 minutes for the dough to rest and the mushrooms to soak.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice flour
ingredients.notes: Divide between the stuffed bánh ít and the ram bases.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually, adjusting until the dough is pliable and not sticky.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Press dry, then crumble or cut into small dice.

ingredients.name: Dried wood-ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, rinse and mince.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Cut into small dice.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Finely slice; divide between the filling and leek oil.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the filling; choose a plant-based product.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the dough and filling.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the filling lightly.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil for frying
ingredients.notes: For deep-frying the ram bases; less will be absorbed.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil for leek
ingredients.notes: For sautéing leek and brushing the steaming leaves.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce for serving
ingredients.notes: Dilute with warm water and chili if desired.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Mince into the dipping sauce; optional.

preparation_steps: Soak the wood-ear mushrooms for 15 minutes, rinse and mince. Press the tofu dry, then finely dice the carrot and leek; set aside the filling ingredients.
Mix the glutinous rice flour with salt and oil. Add warm water a little at a time and knead until smooth and pliable. Cover with a damp towel and rest for 15 minutes.
cooking_steps: Sauté a little leek, then add the carrot and mushrooms and cook for a few minutes. Add the tofu, soy sauce, pepper and some of the salt; cook until dry and let cool.
Divide about half the dough into 12 portions for the ram bases and flatten them. Set on oiled banana leaves and steam for about 15–20 minutes until opaque and cooked through; cool and let dry.
Divide the remaining dough into 12 pieces. Flatten each, add filling, seal and roll into a ball. Steam on banana leaves for about 15–20 minutes until cooked and chewy.
Fry the cooled bases in moderately hot oil until golden and crisp; drain. Set one stuffed bánh ít on each base, drizzle with leek oil and serve with vegetarian soy sauce.

banh-khoai-chay-hue.name: Hue Vegetarian Bánh Khoái
aliases: Hue bánh khoái with tofu and mushrooms
banh-khoai-chay-hue.serving_basis: Eight small bánh khoái, two per person, served hot with greens and vegetarian peanut-soy dip.
banh-khoai-chay-hue.description: Hue vegetarian bánh khoái is a local vegetarian variation. Bếp Việt edits a small batch with a rice-and-wheat-flour batter, tofu, mushrooms, bean sprouts and leek; the dip uses fermented soy, peanuts and sesame instead of the meat-based broth sometimes served with bánh khoái.
banh-khoai-chay-hue.finished_dish: Small golden-crisp pancakes filled with hot mushrooms and tofu and just-wilted bean sprouts, served with fresh greens, sour starfruit and vegetarian peanut-soy dip.
banh-khoai-chay-hue.serving: Fold each pancake in half, cut into pieces and eat hot with mustard greens, lettuce, herbs, starfruit or green banana and vegetarian dipping sauce.
tips: Rest the batter for about 30 minutes so the rice flour hydrates evenly; stir again before ladling it into the pan.
Cook the mushrooms and tofu until their moisture evaporates, then add the bean sprouts near the end so they stay crisp.
Use a small pan and moderately hot oil to crisp the edges without burning the pancake before the filling warms through.
Huế Ngày Nay confirms a vegetarian version but does not prescribe one filling; this tofu-and-mushroom filling is Bếp Việt’s editorial choice.
banh-khoai-chay-hue.image_alt: Golden Hue vegetarian bánh khoái filled with mushrooms, tofu and bean sprouts, served with fresh greens, sour starfruit and a bowl of peanut-soy dip.
banh-khoai-chay-hue.time_note: About 1 hour 15 minutes, including 30 minutes for the batter to rest.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift if lumpy before mixing the batter.

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.notes: Mix with the rice flour to help the edges crisp.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Whisk into the flour until smooth and moderately thin.

ingredients.name: Ground turmeric
ingredients.notes: Adds a light golden color to the batter.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Press dry and cut into small pieces.

ingredients.name: Straw or oyster mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Wipe clean and slice; use one kind or a mix.

ingredients.name: Bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Trim, rinse and drain well.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Thinly slice; divide between the filling and batter.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the batter and filling lightly.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the pancakes; the amount absorbed will be lower.

ingredients.name: Fermented soybean paste
ingredients.notes: Choose a plant-based product for the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush and stir into the vegetarian sauce.

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Crush lightly or leave whole for the sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the saltiness of the fermented soybean paste.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Thin the dipping sauce to a pourable consistency.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Mince; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh greens
ingredients.notes: Mustard greens, lettuce and herbs; rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Sour starfruit or green banana
ingredients.notes: Thinly slice and serve alongside; use either one.

preparation_steps: Whisk the rice flour, wheat flour, salt, turmeric and water until smooth. Rest for 30 minutes, then stir again. Slice the leek, press the tofu dry, slice the mushrooms and rinse the bean sprouts.

Rinse and drain the fresh greens; thinly slice the starfruit or green banana. Crush the peanuts and mix with sesame, fermented soybean paste, sugar, warm water and chili to make a vegetarian dipping sauce.
cooking_steps: Sauté a little leek in oil, add the mushrooms and tofu, season lightly with salt and cook until tender and fairly dry. Set aside.
Heat a small pan with enough oil to coat the base. Ladle in some batter and swirl it into a thin layer; cover for about 1–2 minutes until the surface sets.
Uncover, scatter mushrooms, tofu, bean sprouts and leek over one half of the pancake. Cook until the edge is golden and crisp, fold in half and transfer to drain.
Repeat with the remaining batter and filling. Serve hot with fresh greens, starfruit or green banana and the vegetarian peanut-soy dip.
